# Jubilees Chapter 23 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abraham's Death; The Great Apocalypse

---

**23:1** He placed Jacob's two hands on his eyes and blessed God. He laid his face over Jacob's face and kissed him, and said: "May the LORD God be blessed, and may his name be blessed forever and ever — he who has given me Jacob as a pure son and a holy seed. For he is mine; may he be mine forever and ever."

**23:2** He said: "My son, I command you: keep my commandments and walk in the ways of your father Abraham."

**23:3** Abraham died in the forty-third jubilee, in the sixth year of the seventh week, having lived one hundred and seventy-five years. He completed all the years of his life in peace.

**23:4** For the days of the earliest of the ancients were nineteen jubilees in length. After the Flood they began to fall short of nineteen jubilees, declining and diminishing in jubilees, growing old quickly and reaching the fullness of their days — on account of the manifold tribulations and the wickedness of their ways.

**23:5** All those who are wicked — their days are reckoned, and they are being shortened.

**23:6** In those days, Noah was five hundred years old before he begot Shem. And in his generation Methuselah lived nine hundred and sixty-nine years.

**23:7** For the Most High was angry at the works of the generation of the Flood, for their hearts were corrupt and their thoughts defiled throughout all their days.

**23:8** After the Flood the years of human lives began to diminish: from one hundred years to seventy, from seventy to fifty, from fifty to forty, from forty to thirty-five, from thirty-five to thirty, from thirty to twenty-five, and from twenty-five to twenty.

**23:9** Old age will begin after twenty years, and a person will live out his former days in sorrow and tribulation.

**23:10** There will be no old man — none who is satisfied with his days — for all will be like children and youths.

**23:11** All their works will be done in confusion and with evil intention, and in all their abominable deeds they will corrupt one another.

**23:12** Then one who is ten years old will say: "An eighty-year-old man has not lived out his years; he is like a child of five."

**23:13** And all will be like a child of three years, with no understanding of the path they should walk.

**23:14** In those days, children will begin to study the laws and to search out the commandments, and to return to the path of righteousness.

**23:15** And the days will begin to multiply and increase among those children of men, until their days approach a thousand years and exceed the number of former days.

**23:16** There will be no old man in those days and none who is wearied with age or afflicted with evil; all will be as youths and children throughout all their days.

**23:17** They will live out their whole lives in peace and joy, and there will be no adversary and no evil destroyer — for all their days will be days of blessing and healing.

**23:18** And at that time the LORD will heal his servants, and they will rise up and see great peace, and drive out their adversaries. The righteous will see and give thanks, and rejoice with everlasting joy, and they will see all their judgments and all their curses fall upon their enemies.

**23:19** Their bones will rest in the earth, and their spirits will have great joy, and they will know that it is the LORD who executes judgment and shows mercy to hundreds and thousands and to all who love him.

**23:20** And you, Moses — write down all these words, for thus are they written and thus are they recorded on the heavenly tablets: the divisions of the days of the law and the testimony and the events of the years, their weeks and their jubilees throughout all the years of the world, even until the day of the new creation — when heaven and earth and all their creatures shall be renewed, like the powers of the heavens and like all the creatures of the earth — until the day when the sanctuary of the LORD shall be established in Jerusalem on Mount Zion, and all the luminaries renewed for healing and for peace and for blessing, for all the elect of Israel, from that day forward, for all the days of the earth.

---
*LOGOS notes: The "little apocalypse" of Jubilees 23 is one of the most important eschatological texts in Second Temple literature. The lifespan-reduction sequence (v.8) traces human decline in precise increments. The culminating verse (v.20) connects Moses as recipient, heavenly tablets as source, and the new creation as horizon — a fitting close to the Abraham narrative and a pivot to the Moses frame.*
